question: Is Skillsoft Percipio worth it for corporate training?
text:
Yes—Percipio can be worth it for corporate training, particularly for mid-sized and large organizations that want a broad, centrally managed learning library. But its value depends heavily on what you're trying to train and how actively your L&D team will use it.

Where Percipio is strong

Very broad content library. Skillsoft reports more than 431,000 learning assets covering technology, leadership/business, compliance, AI, cloud, cybersecurity, software development, and more. It includes courses, books, labs, assessments, coaching, bootcamps, and instructor-led options. 
S
Skillsoft Corporation

Good enterprise administration. It supports learning assignments, compliance tracking, certifications, reporting, SSO, and integrations with HR/HCM systems and existing LMS/LXP environments. 
S
Skillsoft Corporation

Strong technology training. If your workforce needs ongoing training in cloud, cybersecurity, software development, data/AI, DevOps, etc., Percipio has a particularly large offering. 
S
Skillsoft Corporation

Skills-oriented approach. Skillsoft has been moving Percipio beyond a traditional course library toward skills mapping, benchmarking, proficiency measurement, personalized recommendations, and AI-assisted learning. 
S
Skillsoft Corporation

Generally positive user feedback. G2 currently shows Percipio at 4.1/5 from 107 reviews. Reviewers frequently praise the breadth of content and ease of use.

Where I'd be cautious

The main issue is that having a huge library isn't the same as having effective training.

Recent G2 feedback mentions limitations around hands-on exercises, video controls/content consistency, administration, and account/support experiences. 
G
G2

I'd therefore be cautious if your goal is:

highly specialized training for your particular business

intensive hands-on technical training

instructor-led development as the primary learning method

highly customized internal processes

training where completion rates and real-world behavior change matter more than content availability

Percipio can provide the infrastructure and content, but you'll still need good learning design, manager involvement, and measurement to turn it into an effective corporate training program.

A practical way to judge the business case

I'd evaluate it against these five questions:

Question	What to look for
Content fit	Do the courses actually cover your top 20–30 required skills?
Usage	Will employees realistically use the library, or will it become "another corporate portal"?
Technical depth	Are labs/simulations sufficient for your technical roles?
Integration	Can it fit cleanly into your existing LMS/HRIS/SSO environment?
Economics	Cost per active learner, not simply cost per licensed employee

The last one is particularly important. A seemingly reasonable enterprise license becomes expensive if only 20–30% of employees actually engage with it.

Bottom line

Percipio makes the most sense when you need breadth, scale, enterprise administration, and continuous skills development. Its extensive technology/business library and newer skills/AI capabilities make it more than just a video-course repository.

I'd want to see a hands-on demo using your actual training requirements before signing a large contract, particularly because user feedback on administration and content depth is mixed.
